activity_context.topic_title: Sums of Finite Geometric Series Given in Sigma Notation

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Sum of a Simplified Geometric Series Given in Sigma Notation
examples.worked_solution:
Since the given series is in the form $\displaystyle{\sum_{n=1}^N a r^{n}},$ it is a geometric series. 

To determine the sum, we use the formula for the sum $S_N$ of a geometric series:

$$
S_N = a_1\dfrac{(1-r^N)}{1-r}
$$

In this case, $r = 4$ and $N = 5.$ We need to figure out the value of $a_1.$

The formula for the $n$th term of the series is

$$
a_n = 3(4)^n,
$$

and therefore we can calculate the first term $a_1$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} & =3(4)^{1} \\  & =12\end{aligned}
$$

If we substitute $a_1 = 12,$ $r = 4,$ and $N = 5$ into the formula for $S_N,$ we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=1}^{5}3(4)^{n} & =12\cdot \frac{(1-{4}^{5})}{1-4} \\  & =-\frac{12}{3}(-1\,023) \\  & =4\,092\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.worked_solution:
Since the given series is in the form ${\sum }_{n=1}^{N}{a}_{1}{r}^{n-1},$ it is a geometric series. 

To determine the sum, we use the formula for the sum ${S}_{N}$ of a geometric series.

$$
{S}_{N}={a}_{1}\frac{(1-{r}^{N})}{1-r}
$$

In this case, ${a}_{1}=\frac{6}{7},$ $r=\frac{1}{3}$ and $N=6.$ If we substitute these values into the formula for ${S}_{N}$, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=1}^{6}\frac{6}{7}{(\frac{1}{3})}^{n-1} & =\frac{6}{7}\cdot \frac{[1-{(\frac{1}{3})}^{6}]}{(1-\frac{1}{3})} \\  & =\frac{6}{7}\cdot \frac{[1-\frac{1}{729}]}{(\frac{2}{3})} \\  & =\frac{6}{7}\cdot \frac{(\frac{728}{729})}{(\frac{2}{3})} \\  & =\frac{6}{7}\cdot \frac{3}{2}\cdot \frac{728}{729} \\  & =\frac{18}{14}\cdot \frac{728}{729} \\  & =\frac{104}{81}\end{aligned}
$$
